solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put off about hot watch returning and rising current

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the phrase before it is read backwards
about means surrounding, so the first word's letters wrap round what follows
something gone off has gone bad or awry, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps
to keep watch is to stand guard

explanation.surface: Someone is put off by a heat-wave watch while a strong current rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off' reads as one phrase meaning deterred, but 'off' is the shuffle signal acting on the first word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An updraught is a column of air flowing upwards, which a glider pilot would call a rising current.

clue.text: Dad's pocketing Roman metal, precious

indicators.note: pocketing means putting something inside, so the first piece holds the second

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for a father
Latin is the language of the Romans

explanation.surface: A father is slipping a valuable Roman coin into his pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', joining father to his action. Platina is an old name for platinum.
explanation.definitionFit: Platina is the early name for platinum, a costly white noble metal used in jewellery.

clue.text: Place for work-out practice with beloved

parts.note: to do something is to practise or perform it
jo is a Scots word for a sweetheart or dear one, as in Burns's John Anderson, my jo

explanation.surface: A gym session done alongside a loved one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dojo is a hall where martial arts such as judo and karate are trained, so a room for physical exercise.

clue.text: Whale as seen entering right or left

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so this piece is placed within the others

parts.note: R is the usual abbreviation for right
taken as written
qua is Latin for 'in the capacity of', i.e. as
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A whale is spotted coming in from one side or the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' here is the Latin word meaning 'in the capacity of', a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A rorqual is a baleen whale with a pleated throat, the family that includes the blue and fin whales.

clue.text: Andante in movement exhausted (7, three words)

indicators.note: putting the letters in motion moves them around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, a musical tempo marking

explanation.surface: A slow movement of a symphony leaves the players worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' looks musical alongside andante, which is a symphony's slow movement, but here it signals the letters moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at an end means used up or finished, as when patience or supplies have run out.

clue.text: Distasteful, smells awfully within, in vacant fashion

indicators.note: within means inside, so the jumbled letters sit inside the first word

parts.note: something gory is bloody and so distasteful

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters come out in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something unpleasant smells dreadful inside, observed with a blank stare.
explanation.definitionFit: Gormless means stupid and lacking sense, so acting gormlessly is behaving with a blank, empty-headed air.

clue.text: Work put into success? Get away (5, two words)

indicators.note: to put something into another thing places it inside, so the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: a hit is a success, like a chart hit
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Is effort what brings success? Go on, be off with you.
explanation.definitionFit: Hop it is a brusque British command telling someone to leave, the same as clear off or scram.

clue.text: What may follow pound payments

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pound ... was the old currency of Scotland
second meaning: a scot is an old tax or share of a charge, as in scot-free

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests money paid in pounds; one sense completes the phrase 'pound ___', the other is the plural of an old word for a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: Scot is an archaic word for a tax or reckoning, and pound Scots names the former Scottish money unit.

clue.text: Group of turtles making hoop by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase says the word is judged by how it is pronounced, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a bail is a hoop or half-hoop, such as the handle of a kettle or the support of a wagon cover

explanation.surface: A cluster of turtles forms a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: BAIL in the sense of a hoop is an unfamiliar meaning listed in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bale is the collective noun for turtles, like a pride of lions or a murder of crows.

clue.text: Trembling, René admits fear — he'll skip middle pages

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the shaken name takes the next piece inside it
something trembling is shaken, so the letters of the name are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
dread is great fear

explanation.surface: A nervous Frenchman confesses to being afraid of something he skips.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: someone who jumps from the start to the final pages of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An end-reader is one who turns to the last chapter first, so skips the whole middle of a book.

clue.text: It often accompanies Indian, one with office

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a pound'
office is an old euphemism for a lavatory, usually in the plural 'offices'

explanation.surface: A sidekick at work comes along with an Indian colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' here means an Indian meal, and 'office' is a polite old word for the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloo is the Hindi for potato, a staple side ingredient in curries such as aloo gobi served at a curry house.

clue.text: Wily thief is capable in card game

parts.note: coon is short for raccoon, an animal known for cunning raids on bins
if someone can, they are able to

explanation.surface: A crafty crook proves skilful at cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooncan is a rummy-type card game for two players, an ancestor of gin rummy.

clue.text: Millet Middle-Easterner rolls round joint

indicators.note: something that rolls turns over, so the word is read backwards
round means surrounding, so the turned word encloses the next piece

parts.note: an Arab is a person from the Middle East
J is slang shorthand for a joint, a cannabis cigarette

explanation.surface: A man from the Middle East rolls a joint, perhaps with millet in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' paired with 'joint' suggests rolling a cigarette, but it turns the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Bajra is the Hindi name for pearl millet, a cereal grain grown widely in India.

clue.text: Brief editorial: unfinished missive including a wound of old

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the shortened word wraps the following pieces
unfinished means lacking its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a missive is a letter
taken as written
dere is an obsolete verb meaning to injure or harm

explanation.surface: A short editorial piece: a half-finished letter about an old injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of old' marks an obsolete Spenserian word, which Azed solvers find in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaderette is a short leading article, the leader being a newspaper's main editorial comment.

clue.text: With which youth starts early, once resigned

indicators.note: asking with which letter a word starts points to just its opening letter

parts.note: the word youth begins with this letter
old can mean early, as in Old English or the old days

explanation.surface: Young people begin early, then later give up.
explanation.walkthrough: Yold is an archaic past participle of yield, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yold is an old past participle of yield, and having yielded is having given in or resigned.

clue.text: Coiled spongey thing tears up flower

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: to tear is to rip
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A twisted sponge-like object pulls a flower out of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears up' reads like uprooting the flower, but it is the word tears turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiraster is a spiral, star-like spicule found in the skeleton of certain sponges.

clue.text: Season returns, almost an end for transmitter

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a season is a time of year

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a term is an end or limit, as in coming to term

explanation.surface: The broadcasting season comes back, nearly marking the end for a radio mast.
explanation.definitionFit: An emitter is anything that sends out signals or radiation, so a transmitter.

clue.text: Nettle giving pointed end, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken sound, so the word goes by pronunciation

parts.note: a peak is the pointed tip of something

explanation.surface: A stinging nettle has a sharp tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nettle' looks like the plant, but here it is the verb meaning to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To pique someone is to irritate or wound their pride, just as to nettle them is to provoke annoyance.

clue.text: Depth may reveal anything but this: see salt at sea

definitions.text: Depth may reveal anything but this

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: In the deep ocean salt is visible, so depth reveals much but not one thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Depth is the opposite of height, and ALTESSE is French for highness; the sea imagery hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: Altesse is the French word for highness, a royal title, and height is the very opposite of depth.

clue.text: Glow from nice candles, flickering, left out

indicators.note: flickering means moving unsteadily, so the remaining letters shift into a new order
a thing left out is omitted, so the letter meaning left is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, minus L for left

explanation.surface: Soft light comes from attractive flickering candles left burning.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the abbreviation for left; it is the letter taken from the fodder before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To incandesce is to become luminous through heat, so to give off a white-hot glow.

clue.text: Titters awkwardly fugal parts being closely grouped

indicators.note: done awkwardly means done clumsily, so the letters land in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Players giggle self-consciously while sections of a fugue are bunched together.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretti, plural of stretto, are fugue passages where entries of the subject overlap in quick succession.

clue.text: Tea brewed as invitation to parley

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
to brew tea is to make it

explanation.surface: A pot of tea is made as a peace offering for talks.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamade is a drum or trumpet signal inviting the enemy to a parley, historically sounded by besieged troops.

clue.text: Callow youths belonging to class

parts.note: a thing in a set belongs to it
a genus is a biological class or kind

explanation.surface: Naive young people belong in a class at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenus are naive, inexperienced young men, the masculine counterpart of the stage ingénue.

clue.text: Leader uncomfortable in the saddle? Not I (10, two words)

indicators.note: being uncomfortable means being unsettled, so the letters shift about
not I tells the solver that the letter I must go

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A captain riding feels sore in the saddle, though not the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests a riding chief; in card games the eldest hand is the player who leads first.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the eldest hand sits on the dealer's left and makes the first lead of play.

clue.text: Left in French city we go fishing

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so this letter goes within the city name

parts.note: Angers is a city in the Loire valley of western France
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Having left for a French city, we spend the day fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers are people who fish with rod and line, so the plural subject 'we' going fishing.

clue.text: Impish youth playin' at the computer?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a street urchin or cheeky child
second meaning: playing video games, with the final G dropped as in playin'

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in playin' is the hint: the second sense is the gaming word with its last letter clipped the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamin is a street urchin, a mischievous neglected child, and gamin' is a clipped spelling of gaming.

clue.text: Prohibition? No go — shut in

indicators.note: no here means without, so the following word is removed

parts.note: an embargo is an official prohibition on trade
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: A ban means you cannot leave: you are confined.
explanation.definitionFit: Embar is an archaic verb meaning to enclose or imprison, so to confine someone behind bars.

clue.text: Scots furious? What he's in includes daughter

indicators.note: includes means takes inside, so the first word holds the next letter

parts.note: the man who is furious is in a rage
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is livid, and the cause of his temper involves his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' refers back to the furious Scot of the definition: the state he is in is a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Radge is Scots and northern English dialect for wild, crazy or violently angry.

clue.text: Ignoring ad Madam's let out bright red underwear

indicators.note: let out like a seam, the letters are loosened and rearranged
ignoring means leaving out, so those two letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written, to be removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brothel madam lets out scarlet lingerie, without advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Madam's supplies the S needed in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Stammel is a coarse woollen cloth, usually dyed red, formerly worn for undergarments and petticoats.

clue.text: Monument in honour of doctor

parts.note: as in a toast or dedication: to the memory of
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A memorial erected to honour a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomb is a burial vault or grave monument, often grand, built over the dead.

clue.text: Slow mover in university, being queasy after quitting sea

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

indicators.note: after something has quit it has left, so those letters are removed

parts.note: nausea is the state of being queasy
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: A student who takes their time feels seasick after leaving the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: NAUSEA loses its final three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The unau is the two-toed sloth of South America, an animal famous for moving extremely slowly.

clue.text: Edison's short version? It may take a lot of getting through

definitions.text: It may take a lot of getting through

parts.note: Tom is the short form of Thomas, the inventor's first name
the surname shortened to its initial

explanation.surface: The inventor's abridged works might still be a heavy read.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Edison cut down becomes Tom E., first name shortened, surname reduced to an initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large, heavy book, the kind a reader needs real stamina to finish.

clue.text: Excerpt from secret annals revealed in police station overseas

indicators.note: an excerpt is a passage lifted from a longer text, so the letters run inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A passage from classified records turns up at a foreign police station.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanna (or thana) is a police station in India, a word from Hindi.

clue.text: In e.g. juillet mineral's seen to sparkle

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the mineral goes within the French word

parts.note: juillet (July) is an example of été, the French for summer
mica is a glittering silicate mineral that splits into thin sheets

explanation.surface: In July a mineral glints in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: Juillet is the French July, a summer month, so it exemplifies été.
explanation.definitionFit: Emicate is a rare verb meaning to sparkle or flash out, from the Latin for shining forth.

clue.text: Pa's gone round the bend, causing thump

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so the father holds the bend

parts.note: pa and dad are both words for a father
a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: Father has gone mad and lashes out with a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone round the bend' is slang for gone mad, but here the bend is a U-shaped one.
explanation.definitionFit: Daud is a Scots word for a heavy blow or thump, also spelt dawd.

clue.text: She likes to appear fastidious, and prim around European Union

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the first word wraps the abbreviation

parts.note: a precise person is prim and exact
EU is the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A woman who wants to seem fussy and proper in Brussels circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A précieuse is a woman who affects refined, overly delicate manners, after the salon ladies mocked by Molière.
